iucn.long: Listed as Least Concern on the IUCN Red List.

overview.text: The Ladder Snake is a harmless rat snake found only in south-western Europe, common in Portugal and Spain. It is named after the ladder-like pattern on the backs of young snakes - *scalaris* is Latin for "of a ladder".

identification.label: Adults
identification.text: Yellowish to dark brown, with two darker stripes running along the body from the neck to the tail.

variation.label: Young
variation.text: Juveniles are brighter, yellow to light brown, with the black "ladder" pattern along the back. The pattern fades with age, leaving the simpler two-striped adult pattern.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: South-western Europe: the Iberian Peninsula and the Mediterranean south of France.

diet.text: A study of 368 snakes in Spain found that adults feed almost only on warm-blooded prey - mainly mammals, nearly 95% of the diet by weight - with a few birds; adults climb trees and buildings to raid nests. Young snakes eat small lizards, baby rodents, spiders and grasshoppers.

funfacts.text: Only young Ladder Snakes show the ladder pattern that gives the species its name.
